Optimizer Playground

Pick a differentiable objective, an optimizer, and a learning rate. The contour plot shows the parameter path, and the loss plot shows how fast the objective falls over time.

Run Summary

What This Shows

Differentiable f is enough
Step size matters
Noisy gradients are estimates
Orange is the optimizer path, green marks the start, and red marks the final point. The noise slider only affects the SGD-style mini-batch approximation.

Discussion Questions

  • Why is it enough for the objective f to be differentiable, even if we do not derive every update by hand?
  • What happens when the learning rate is too small, too large, or in a useful middle range?
  • How does the noisy SGD-style path differ from full gradient descent on the same surface?
  • When does Adam reach a low-loss region faster or more stably than plain gradient descent?
  • What parts of these trajectories would a standard library need from the forward pass in order to compute gradients?
